title: Operating, Investing & Financing Activities
description: Classify cash receipts and payments into the three major cash flow categories.
html:
Operating activities

Operating activities generally include cash effects associated with transactions that enter into the determination of net income, except where classified elsewhere under applicable guidance.

Common examples

  • Cash collected from customers
  • Cash paid to suppliers
  • Cash paid to employees
  • Other operating cash receipts and payments

Investing activities

Investing activities generally involve acquiring and disposing of long-term assets and certain investments.

Examples

  • Purchase of property, plant and equipment
  • Cash proceeds from sale of equipment
  • Making certain loans to other entities
  • Collection of principal on certain loans

Financing activities

Financing activities generally involve obtaining resources from owners and creditors and returning resources to them.

Examples

  • Issuing common stock for cash
  • Borrowing cash through debt
  • Repaying debt principal
  • Repurchasing company shares for cash
  • Cash dividends paid to shareholders

Classification example

Buy Equipment

Investing outflow

Issue Stock

Financing inflow

Collect from Customers

Operating inflow

Repay Loan Principal

Financing outflow

CPA habit

Don't classify a cash flow merely because "cash went in" or "cash went out."

Ask what economic activity caused the cash flow.

quiz.prompt: A company pays $70,000 cash to purchase equipment. How is the payment generally classified on the statement of cash flows?
quiz.explanation: Cash paid to acquire property, plant and equipment is generally an investing cash outflow.

objectives: Explain operating, investing & financing activities and its underlying principles.
Apply the topic to a financial-reporting scenario.
Evaluate common errors and their financial-statement effects.
